info.title: Python TDD workflow with requirement XML integration

parts.text:
"You are inspecting a Python project inside a container at /app.

READ ONLY. Do not create, modify or delete any file under /app.
Any write there invalidates this run.

A developer is about to work on the task described below.

\"
<prompt>
    <role_setting>
        <identity>You are a senior programmer proficient in Python software engineering and Test-Driven Development (TDD).</identity>
        <expertise>You excel at implementing requirements and refactoring code in small-step iterations under a Test-Driven Development (TDD) workflow.</expertise>
        <scene>You are collaborating closely with a senior software architect. The architect produces incremental requirement documents based on the functional gaps of the current code; you are responsible for understanding the content of this document and implementing the requirements to change the status of target tests from non-passed to passed.</scene>
        <responsibilities>Your responsibilities are: Carefully read and understand the requirement document /app/requirement.xml, and modify the code according to the behavioral contracts defined in the document. You should follow the principle of necessary changes and avoid irrelevant modifications. You are prohibited from executing test actively.</responsibilities>
    </role_setting>

    <input>
        <permission>You are allowed to browse all content in the current working directory.</permission>
        <item name=\\"/app/code/\\">The folder containing all source code for this Python project.</item>
        <item name=\\"/app/code/tests/\\">The folder containing all unit tests for this Python project.</item>
        <item name=\\"/app/requirement.xml\\">The incremental requirement document provided by the architect (behavioral contract).</item>
    </input>

    <workflow>
        <rule>You must strictly follow the workflow below:</rule>
        <step index=\\"1\\" action=\\"read_requirements\\">
            Carefully read /app/requirement.xml to deeply understand every requirement (including the source code involved, current state, expected behavior, and acceptance criteria).
        </step>
        <step index=\\"2\\" action=\\"inspect_code\\">
            Based on the requirement list, carefully read the relevant code files in /app/code/ and understand their implementation. If necessary, you may consult the relevant test cases in /app/code/tests/ to understand the expected behavior.
        </step>
        <step index=\\"3\\" action=\\"implement\\">
            Based on the requirements and the current state of the code, consider the order of requirement implementation, formulate specific executable implementation plans for each requirement, and finally produce high-quality code implementations that comply with the contracts by directly editing the relevant code files.
        </step>
    </workflow>

    <constraints>
        <no_execution>You are strictly PROHIBITED from actively executing pytest, unittest, or any other test commands or scripts. Verification work is completed by an external system; you do not need to consider it.</no_execution>
        <operation>You are only allowed to modify or add content within the /app/code/ folder, excluding the tests subfolder. It is strictly PROHIBITED to make any changes to the /app/requirement.xml file or the /app/code/tests/ folder.</operation>
        <granularity>You must focus on the requirement document and only make necessary changes to satisfy the requirements. You should not expand the scope on your own or over-develop.</granularity>
    </constraints>

    <output>
        <product>Your modified codebase (changes under /app/code/). Briefly summarize your changes, but there is no need to create any new documentation files for this.</product>
    </output>
</prompt>

\"

Read enough of /app/code to answer concretely, then name 3 to 5
plausible FUTURE tasks that could reasonably follow this one in THIS codebase.
Refer to real files, functions or modules you actually read. Do not solve the
task, and do not write any file."

I'll analyze the Python project structure and requirements to understand what tasks might follow.

First, let me examine the project structure and the requirement document:

281:             assert isinstance(dest, tuple)
282:             if not dest[1].name:
283:                 raise ValueError("The name was not provided for one of the outputs.")
284: 
285:             path = _get_outputs_path(dest[1])
286:             _write_to_path(path, "")

289: def _write_to_path(path: Path, output_value: Any, dumper: Callable = serialize) -> None:
290:     """Write the output_value as serialized text to the provided path. Create the necessary parent directories."""

292:     if output_string is not None:
293:         path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
294:         path.write_text(output_string)

60: def _ignore_unmatched_kwargs(f: Callable) -> Callable:
61:     """Make function ignore unmatched kwargs.

63:     If the function already has the catch all **kwargs, do nothing.
64:     """
65:     if _contains_var_kwarg(f):
66:         return f
67: 
68:     @functools.wraps(f)

70:         # filter out kwargs that are not part of the function signature
71:         # and transform them to the correct type
72:         filtered_kwargs = {key: _parse(value, key, f) for key, value in kwargs.items() if _is_kwarg_of(key, f)}
73:         return f(**filtered_kwargs)
74: 
75:     return inner

77: 
78: def _contains_var_kwarg(f: Callable) -> bool:
79:     """Tells whether the given callable contains a keyword argument."""
80:     return any(param.kind == inspect.Parameter.VAR_KEYWORD for param in inspect.signature(f).parameters.values())
81: 
82: 
83: def _is_kwarg_of(key: str, f: Callable) -> bool:
84:     """Tells whether the given `key` identifies a keyword argument of the given callable."""
85:     param = inspect.signature(f).parameters.get(key)
86:     return param is not None and (
87:         param.kind is inspect.Parameter.KEYWORD_ONLY or param.kind is inspect.Parameter.POSITIONAL_OR_KEYWORD
88:     )

91: def _parse(value: str, key: str, f: Callable) -> Any:
92:     """Parse a value to the correct type.
93: 
94:     Args:
95:         value: The value to parse.
96:         key: The name of the kwarg.
97:         f: The function to parse the value for.
98: 
99:     Returns:
100:         The parsed value.

102:     """
103:     if _is_str_kwarg_of(key, f) or _is_artifact_loaded(key, f) or _is_output_kwarg(key, f):
104:         return value
105:     try:
106:         type_ = _get_unannotated_type(key, f)
107:         loaded_json_value = json.loads(value)
108: 
109:         if not type_:
110:             return loaded_json_value
111: 
112:         _pydantic_mode = int(os.environ.get("hera__pydantic_mode", _PYDANTIC_VERSION))
113:         if _pydantic_mode == 1:

131:     if type_ is None:

138:     if func_param_annotation := _get_function_param_annotation(key, f):

143: def _is_artifact_loaded(key: str, f: Callable) -> bool:
144:     """Check if param `key` of function `f` is actually an Artifact that has already been loaded."""
145:     if param_annotation := _get_function_param_annotation(key, f):
146:         if (artifact := get_workflow_annotation(param_annotation)) and isinstance(artifact, Artifact):
147:             return artifact.loader == ArtifactLoader.json.value
148:     return False

151: def _is_output_kwarg(key: str, f: Callable) -> bool:
152:     """Check if param `key` of function `f` is an output Artifact/Parameter."""
153:     if param_annotation := _get_function_param_annotation(key, f):
154:         if param_or_artifact := get_workflow_annotation(param_annotation):
155:             return bool(param_or_artifact.output)
156:     return False

159: def _map_function_annotations(function: Callable, template_inputs: Dict[str, str]) -> Dict:
160:     """Parse annotations to substitute values from Argo for the function parameters.
161: 
162:     For Parameter inputs:
163:     * if the Parameter has a "name", replace it with the function parameter name
164:     * otherwise use the function parameter name as-is
165:     * use the Parameter loader if provided
166:     For Parameter outputs:
167:     * update value to a Path object from the value_from.path value, or the default if not provided
168: 
169:     For Artifact inputs:
170:     * load the Artifact according to the given ArtifactLoader
171:     For Artifact outputs:
172:     * update value to a Path object
173:     """
174:     if _contains_var_kwarg(function):
175:         return template_inputs
176: 
177:     function_kwargs: Dict[str, Any] = {}
178: 
179:     # Iterate over the _function parameters_ and map the template inputs to them
180:     # e.g. for `function=func(param: Annotated[int, Parameter(name="my-param")])`,
181:     # and template_inputs={"my-param": "5"}, the function_kwargs will be {"param": 5}
182:     for func_param_name, func_param in inspect.signature(function).parameters.items():
183:         if param_or_artifact := get_workflow_annotation(func_param.annotation):
184:             if isinstance(param_or_artifact, Parameter):
185:                 if param_or_artifact.output:
186:                     function_kwargs[func_param_name] = get_annotated_output_param(param_or_artifact)
187:                 else:
188:                     param_value = get_annotated_input_param(func_param_name, param_or_artifact, template_inputs)

190:                     function_kwargs[func_param_name] = load_param_input(param_value, param_or_artifact.loads)
191:             else:
192:                 function_kwargs[func_param_name] = get_annotated_artifact_value(param_or_artifact)

194:         elif not is_subscripted(func_param.annotation) and issubclass(func_param.annotation, (InputV1, InputV2)):

196:             function_kwargs[func_param_name] = map_runner_input(func_param.annotation, template_inputs)

198:         else:

200:             function_kwargs[func_param_name] = template_inputs[func_param_name]

204: def _runner(entrypoint: str, template_inputs_list: List) -> Any:
205:     """Run the function defined by the entrypoint with the given list of kwargs.
206: 
207:     Args:

209:         template_inputs_list: A list of dicts with "name" and "value" keys, to be mapped to the kwargs of the function.

211:     Returns:
212:         The result of the function or `None` if the outputs are to be saved.
213:     """
214:     # import the module and get the function
215:     module, function_name = entrypoint.split(":")

238:     if _pydantic_mode == 2:
239:         from pydantic import ConfigDict, validate_call  # type: ignore
240: 
241:         function = validate_call(config=ConfigDict(arbitrary_types_allowed=True))(function)
242:     else:

244:             from pydantic.v1 import validate_arguments
245:         else:

247:                 from pydantic import validate_arguments
248:             else:
249:                 from pydantic.v1 import validate_arguments
250: 
251:         function = validate_arguments(config=dict(smart_union=True, arbitrary_types_allowed=True))(function)
252: 
253:     function = _ignore_unmatched_kwargs(function)

255:     output_annotations = _extract_return_annotation_output(function)

257:     if output_annotations:

259:         # outputs should be written to within the function itself.
260:         try:

262:         except Exception as e:

266: 
267:     return function(**function_kwargs)
